senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; רָעָה or רָעַע to join) friend, associate, neighbor.
units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1:32">Ex. R. s. 1</cite> (ref. to <he>ר̇ע̇וא̇ל̇</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 2:18">Ex. II, 18</cite>) <he>נעשה ר̇יע̇ לא̇ל̇</he> he (Jethro) became a friend of God (converted).

<cite ref="Bava Batra 19a:12">B. Bath. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>יגיד עליו רֵיעוֹ וכ׳</he> (adopted from <cite ref="Job 36:33">Job XXXVI, 33</cite>) let its neighbor (an analogous passage) interpret it, as here (<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 2:1">B. Bath. II, 1</cite>) rocks are mentioned, and the same rule applies to sand, so there (<cite ref="Shabbat 4a">Sabb. I</cite>V, sand is mentioned, and rocks are implied; <cite ref="Yevamot 31b:2">Yeb. 31ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Metzia 31a:5">B. Mets. 31ᵃ</cite>.
Ab. ch. VI נקרא ר׳ he is called a friend (of God); a. fr.—Esp. lover, paramour, contrad. to בעל.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 32:2">Ex. R. s. 32</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Jeremiah 3:20">Jer. III, 20</cite>) <he>מאישה לא נאמר אלא מֵרֵעָהּ מה אשה … בבעלה אלא ברֵעָהּ וכ׳</he> it does not say, ‘to her husband’, but ‘to her lover’, as a woman cannot rebel against her husband, but can deny her lover, because there is no marriage contract between them, so said the Lord to Israel, <he>לא כרע עשיתוני … אלא</he> you have not treated me as a husband, but as a lover; a. e.—Pl. <cite ref="T00674"><he>רֵיעִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="T00673"><he>רֵעִ׳</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Taanit 25b:8">Taan. 25ᵇ</cite> deep says to deep, <he>אַבַּע מימיך קול שני ר׳ וכ׳</he> let thy waters well forth, I hear the voice of two (companies of) friends (the songs accompanying the libation of wine and that of water).

<cite ref="Nedarim 40a:4">Ned. 40ᵃ</cite> <he>שיזדמנו לו ר׳ כנעמן … ואל יזדמנו ר׳ כשלמה וכ׳</he> that he have friends (to counsel him) as Naaman bad, who caused him to be healed of his leprosy, and not friends as Rehoboam had, who caused the division of his kingdom; a. e.
